f.title: Definition: serious adverse reaction
f.statement: A serious adverse reaction is a harmful and unintended reaction to a medicine that results in death, is life-threatening, results in persistent or significant incapacity/disability, requires hospitalisation or prolongs inpatient hospitalisation, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or results in another medically significant condition.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder and sponsor (for seriousness assessment)
rows.quote: A “serious adverse reaction” shall mean a harmful and unintended reaction to a medicine which shall: - result in death; - is life-threatening; - result in persistent or significant incapacity/disability; - requires hospitalization or prolonged impatient hospitalization; - is a congenial anomaly/birth defect; - result in other medically significant condition;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Definition: unexpected adverse reaction
f.statement: An unexpected adverse reaction is a reaction whose nature, severity or outcome is not described in the summary of product characteristics and/or, for investigational medicines, the investigator's brochure.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder and sponsor (for expectedness assessment)
rows.quote: An “unexpected adverse reaction” shall mean a reaction to a medicine whose nature, severity or outcome are not described in the summary of product characteristics and/or investigator’s brochure for investigational medicines;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Mandatory reporting is done by the MAH and the clinical trial sponsor
f.statement: For the Rulebook, mandatory reporting means reporting of adverse reactions occurring during clinical trials or after marketing authorisation, and it is carried out by the marketing authorisation holder and the sponsor of a clinical trial.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder; clinical trial sponsor
rows.quote: “Mandatory reporting” shall mean reporting of adverse reactions to a medicine occurring during clinical trials or in the period after obtaining an authorization to place a medicine on the market. Mandatory reporting shall, for the purpose of the Rulebook, be carried out by the marketing authorization holder and sponsor of a clinical trial
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Protect reporter identity: share it only with the Agency in the ICSR
f.statement: When an adverse reaction is reported through the MAH, the MAH must protect the reporter's identity: reporter information may be given only to the Agency in the ICSR and must not be disclosed to third parties.
f.clause: II.3 Information about the reporter, Article 7
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Data integrity & records

rows.quote: When reporting an adverse reaction to a medicine through the marketing authorization holder, the marketing authorization holder shall be obliged to protect the identity of the reporter by submitting information about the reporter in the ICSR exclusively to the Agency, and he or she shall not reveal it to the third parties.
rows.location: II.3 Information about the reporter, Article 7
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Organise continuous monitoring of adverse reactions
f.statement: The MAH must organise continuous monitoring of adverse reactions to its medicines.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall be obliged to organize continuous monitoring of adverse reactions to a medicine.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Have, maintain and upgrade an appropriate PV system for Serbian products
f.statement: The MAH must have an appropriate pharmacovigilance system enabling monitoring and supervision of the medicines it holds authorisations for in the Republic of Serbia, take appropriate measures where necessary, and ensure continuous maintenance and upgrading of the system.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall be obliged to have an established appropriate pharmacovigilance system which shall enable monitoring and supervision of one or more medicines he or she holds the authorization for in the Republic of Serbia, and to conduct appropriate measures, if necessary. The marketing authorization holder shall ensure continuous maintenance and upgrading of the pharmacovigilance system.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Have a DDPS available to pharmacovigilance inspection
f.statement: The MAH must have a Detailed Description of the Pharmacovigilance System (DDPS) for the medicines it holds authorisations for in Serbia, and it should be available to the pharmacovigilance inspection.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall be obliged to have DDPS for one or more medicines which he or she holds the marketing authorization for in the Republic of Serbia, and which should be made available to the inspection in the field of pharmacovigilance.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Employ a resident person responsible for pharmacovigilance full-time
f.statement: The MAH must conclude an open-ended full-time employment agreement with an appropriately qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance who resides in the Republic of Serbia.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall be obliged to conclude an agreement for the full-time employment on the open-end basis with a person that has appropriate qualifications and who is responsible for pharmacovigilance (hereinafter referred to as the “person responsible for pharmacovigilance”), and residing in the Republic of Serbia.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Appoint the person responsible for PV for all products and inform the Agency
f.statement: The MAH must appoint a person responsible for pharmacovigilance for all its medicines authorised in Serbia and inform the Agency.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall appoint a person responsible for pharmacovigilance for all medicines which he or she holds the marketing authorization for in the Republic of Serbia, and inform the Agency about this.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: A resident deputy may be appointed and covers all RPV activities in absence
f.statement: The MAH may appoint a deputy, resident in Serbia, authorised to carry out the activities of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance, and must inform the Agency; the deputy assumes all the RPV's activities in the RPV's absence.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder may also appoint and/or determine another person who shall have authorizations to conduct activities of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance and residing in the Republic of Serbia (hereinafter referred to as the “deputy”), and inform the Agency about this. The deputy referred to in paragraph 3 of the Article shall assume all the activities of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance in his or her absence.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: RPV and deputy: medical, pharmacy or dental degree and PV education
f.statement: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance and the deputy must hold a degree from a faculty of medicine, pharmacy or dentistry and have appropriate pharmacovigilance education, including completed trainings by competent agencies in PV notions, spontaneous reporting, reporting and assessment of ADR reports, PSUR and RMP, and Serbian and EU PV regulations.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance and deputy (MAH ensures)
rows.quote: Activities of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance and/or the deputy may be conducted by a person graduated from the faculty of medicine, pharmacy or dentistry, and who shall have appropriate education in the field of pharmacovigilance. The person responsible for pharmacovigilance and/or the deputy shall have completed trainings in the following areas of pharmacovigilance organized the competent agencies: 1) Notions of pharmacovigilance; 2) Spontaneous reporting of adverse reactions to a medicine; 3) The method of reporting adverse reactions to a medicine and assessment of reports on adverse reactions to a medicine; 4) PSUR and RMP; 5) The knowledge of regulations in the field of pharmacovigilance (Republic of Serbia and European Union).
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: RPV and deputy: continuous PV training with records
f.statement: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance and the deputy must attend continuous professional training in pharmacovigilance, and records should be kept.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance and deputy
rows.quote: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance and/or the deputy shall attend continuous professional trainings in the field of pharmacovigilance, and records should be kept of this.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Submit the RPV notification dossier to the Agency
f.statement: When notifying the person responsible for pharmacovigilance and/or the deputy, the MAH must submit: its statement of appointment; the RPV's CV; copy of the graduation certificate; copy of the PV training certificate; evidence of residence; 24/7 contact details; and evidence of permanent employment with the MAH.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall, when reporting on the person responsible for pharmacovigilance and/or the deputy, submit to the Agency the following as mandatory: 1) The statement of the marketing authorization holder about the appointment of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance; 2) CV of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance; 3) A photocopy of an appropriate certificate of graduation; 4) A photocopy of a certificate of passed training in the field of pharmacovigilance; 5) Evidence of the place of residence of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance; 6) 24/7 contact information of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance; 7) Evidence of establishing permanent employment of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance with the marketing authorization holder.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: No deputy: explain and state the RPV is the 24/7 contact
f.statement: If the MAH does not appoint a deputy, it must inform the Agency, with an explanation and a statement that the person responsible for pharmacovigilance will be the 24/7 contact ensuring proper operation of the PV system.
f.exceptions: Applies only when no deputy is appointed

rows.quote: If the marketing authorization holder shall not appoint a deputy of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance, he or she shall be obliged to inform the Agency about this, by submitting an explanation and a statement that the person responsible for pharmacovigilance shall be the 24/7 contact in ensuring proper operation of the pharmacovigilance system.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: RPV responsibilities: PV system, safety profile, 24/7 and inspection contact
f.statement: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance is responsible for establishing, maintaining and managing the PV system; monitors the safety profile and all safety issues of all the MAH's medicines authorised in Serbia; is the 24/7 contact for the Agency; and is the contact for pharmacovigilance inspection.
f.clause: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance shall do the following in accordance with the Law: 1) be responsible for establishing, maintaining and managing the pharmacovigilance system; 2) monitor the safety profile and all safety issues related to all the medicines which the marketing authorization holder holds the authorization for in the Republic of Serbia; 3) be the 24/7 contact for the Agency; 4) be the contact for the inspection in the field of pharmacovigilance.
rows.location: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: RPV ensures core PV system parts operate
f.statement: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance must monitor the PV system so that at least the following operate: collection of all suspected ADRs reported to MAH associates with full access at a minimum of one location in Serbia; preparing and forwarding ICSRs, PSURs, RMPs, the DDPS and PASS reports to the Agency; and continuous overall post-marketing PV assessment.
f.clause: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
f.processes: Safety governance; Safety intake & collection; Submission operations; Benefit–risk review

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance shall monitor the pharmacovigilance system in order to ensure operation of at least the following parts of the system: 1) Establishing and managing the system which shall ensure that information on all suspected adverse reactions reported to the associates of the marketing authorization holder are collected in the manner which shall ensure full access at a minimum one location in the Republic of Serbia; 2) Developing, acquiring and forwarding the following safety documents submitted to the Agency: ICSR, PSUR, RMP, DDPS, PASS report; 3) Continuous overall assessment of pharmacovigilance of a medicine after it has been placed on the market;
rows.location: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: RPV ensures risk minimisation monitoring and full, prompt answers to the Agency
f.statement: The RPV must also ensure monitoring of the outcome of risk minimisation activities defined in the RMP or of marketing authorisation conditions; that Agency requests for additional benefit-risk information are answered fully and without delay, including sales volumes and numbers of prescriptions; and that all relevant benefit-risk information, including post-marketing use assessments, is submitted to the Agency.
f.clause: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Submission operations; Benefit–risk review

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: 4) Monitoring of the outcome of activities of risk minimization defined within the RMP, or of the marketing authorization conditions; 5) Ensuring that any requirements of the Agency for additional information necessary for the assessment of benefits and risks of a medicine are fully presented and without delay, including information on the amount of sale and number of issued prescriptions for a medicine; 6) Submitting the Agency all the relevant information on the assessment of benefits and risks of a medicine, including information on the assessment of medicine administration after it is being marketed.
rows.location: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: RPV ensures quality, SOPs, databases, contracts, compliance and training
f.statement: The RPV's activities must also ensure proper operation of all other PV system segments, including quality assurance control, SOPs, databases, contract programmes, compliance (quality, completeness and timeliness of serious ADR reporting, PSUR frequency), review and assessment of individual ADR reports, and training of associates.
f.clause: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Partner & vendor oversight; Training & competency; Safety system configuration

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: Activities of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance of the marketing authorization holder shall also ensure proper operation of the pharmacovigilance system in all other segments including quality assurance control, standard operating procedures, data bases, contract programs, compliance with the provisions e.g. quality, comprehensiveness and timeliness in reporting serious adverse reactions to a medicine, frequency of submission of PSURs, review and assessment of individual reports of adverse reactions and training of associates in pharmacovigilance.
rows.location: II.6 Person responsible for pharmacovigilance, Article 16
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Maintain a system to collect, process, assess and store all AE/ADR information worldwide
f.statement: The RPV must establish and maintain a system for collecting, processing, assessing and storing information on all adverse events or reactions reported to the manufacturer, MAH or persons promoting the medicine, or described in the scientific literature, regardless of geographical origin.
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up; Data integrity & records

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: 1) Establish and maintain the system for collection, processing, assessment and storing of the information on all adverse events or reactions to a medicine reported to the manufacturer of a medicine, marketing authorization holder, persons promoting a medicine, or on adverse events and/or reactions to a medicine described in the scientific literature, regardless of the geographical origin of the source of information;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Propose safety measures and answer Agency requests fully and timely
f.statement: The RPV must propose to the Agency measures to be taken for safety reasons and provide comprehensive and timely replies and information needed to assess the medicine's safety and the health risk during its use.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: 2) Propose measures to the Agency which should be taken for safety reasons, and provide comprehensive and timely replies and required information needed for the assessment of medicine safety and of a health risk during its administration;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Report all domestic adverse reactions to the Agency
f.statement: The RPV must report to the Agency all adverse reactions (and suspicions) occurring in Serbia, regardless of seriousness and expectedness, including any suspected transmission of an infectious agent via a medicine.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: 3) Report to the Agency on all adverse reactions to a medicine, regardless of the severity and expectancy, and/or suspicion of them, including any suspected transmission of an infectious agent through a medicine that has occurred on the territory of the Republic of Serbia;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Submit serious domestic ADRs within 15 days of first receipt
f.statement: The RPV must report to the Agency all serious adverse reactions (and suspicions) occurring in Serbia, including suspected transmission of an infectious agent, no later than 15 days from first receipt of the information; the period covers initial and subsequent reporting.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.deadline: No later than 15 days from first receipt of the information
rows.quote: 4) Report to the Agency on all serious adverse reactions to a medicine, and/or suspicion of them, including any suspected transmission of an infectious agent through a medicine that has occurred on the territory of the Republic of Serbia, not later than 15 days from the date of the first receipt of the information, whereas the prescribed period shall include initial and subsequent reporting;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

deadline_rule.clock_start: the date of the first receipt of the information
deadline_rule.applies_to: serious adverse reactions occurring in Serbia

f.title: Submit foreign serious unexpected ADRs within 15 days
f.statement: The RPV must report to the Agency all serious unexpected adverse reactions (and suspicions) reported outside Serbia, including suspected transmission of an infectious agent outside Serbia, immediately or no later than 15 days from first receipt; the period covers initial and subsequent reporting.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.deadline: Immediately, no later than 15 days from first receipt of the information
rows.quote: 5) Report to the Agency on all serious, unexpected adverse reactions to a medicine, and/or suspicion of them, that have been reported outside the territory of the Republic of Serbia, including any suspected transmission of an infectious agent through a medicine that has occurred outside the territory of the Republic of Serbia, immediately or not later than 15 days from the date of the first receipt of the information, whereas the prescribed period shall include initial and subsequent reporting;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. f.title: Report ADRs from MAH-funded post-marketing non-interventional studies
f.statement: The RPV must report adverse reactions occurring in post-marketing non-interventional (pharmacoepidemiological) studies financed by the manufacturer or MAH in line with the domestic, serious domestic and foreign serious unexpected reporting rules.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: 6) Report in accordance with items 3), 4) and 5) of the Article on adverse reactions to a medicine during the post-marketing non-interventional clinical trial of a medicine (pharmacoepidemiological trial) financed by the manufacturer or marketing authorization holder;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Report medication errors, overdose, abuse, off-label use, lack of efficacy and interactions
f.statement: The RPV must report to the Agency all suspected medical errors, overdose, addiction, abuse and unauthorised (off-label) use, absence of therapeutic efficacy and clinically significant interactions.

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: 7) Report to the Agency on all suspected medical errors, overdose, addiction, abuse and unauthorized administration of a medicine, absence of therapeutic efficacy of a medicine and clinically significant interactions.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Submit ICSRs on the CIOMS-I form
f.statement: The RPV must make the reports under Article 17 items 3-7 by submitting the ICSR on the CIOMS-I form (Attachment 7).

rows.actor: Person responsible for pharmacovigilance (of the MAH)
rows.quote: The person responsible for pharmacovigilance shall conduct the activities set out in items 3)-7) of the Article by submitting the ICSR on the CIOMS-I form.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: ICSR minimum content: reporter/MAH, identifiable patient, suspect medicine, reaction
f.statement: An ICSR must contain at least: the reporter and/or MAH; an identifiable patient (initials, year of birth and gender); the suspect medicine (trade name and/or INN); and the adverse reaction.
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; ICSR quality control

rows.quote: The ICSR shall contain at least the information on the following: 1) The party reporting an adverse reaction and/or marketing authorization holder; 2) The patient that can be identified (by initials, year of birth and gender); 3) The name of the medicine that is suspected to have caused an adverse reaction (trade name and/or INN); 4) An adverse reaction to a medicine.
data_elements: suspect medicine trade name or INN
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Inform the Agency before or when releasing PV information to the public
f.statement: The MAH must not provide pharmacovigilance information about a medicine to the public or professionals without informing the Agency beforehand or at the same time; such information must be objective and not misleading.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall not provide the general public and professional community with the information relating to the pharmacovigilance of a medicine without previously or simultaneously informing the Agency about this. The information on pharmacovigilance referred to in paragraph 1 of the Article, which the marketing authorization holder shall provide to the public, shall be objective and/or the information shall not have the misleading character.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Create the DDPS and submit it to the Agency
f.statement: The MAH is responsible for creating the DDPS and submitting it to the Agency; a MAH whose manufacturer is outside Serbia must submit a DDPS describing both the manufacturer's global PV system and the MAH's local Serbian PV system.
f.clause: II.7 Detailed description of the pharmacovigilance system, Article 20

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall be responsible for creating the DDPS document and submitting it to the Agency. The marketing authorization holder, whose manufacturer is based outside the Republic of Serbia, shall submit the document referred to in paragraph 1 of the Article, which shall contain a description of the global pharmacovigilance system made by the manufacturer and a description of the local pharmacovigilance system of the marketing authorization holder in the Republic of Serbia.
rows.location: II.7 Detailed description of the pharmacovigilance system, Article 20
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Generic MAH: explain absence of global PV description in cover letter
f.statement: As an exception, a MAH of a generic medicine must explain in the cover letter to the Agency the absence of a description of the manufacturer's global PV system in the DDPS.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder of a generic medicine
rows.quote: As an exception, a holder of the marketing authorization for a generic medicine shall in a cover letter submitted to the Agency provide an explanation as opposed to the absence of a description of the global pharmacovigilance system created by the manufacturer in the DDPS document.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: DDPS covers all products; product-specific appendix with MA application; Serbian or English
f.statement: The DDPS must cover all medicines the MAH holds authorisations for in Serbia; where a medicine has particularities in its PV system, an appendix must be submitted with the marketing authorisation documentation. The DDPS and appendices must be in Serbian or English, with contents per Attachment 1.

rows.quote: The DDPS shall refer to all the medicines which the marketing authorization holder has the authorization for in the Republic of Serbia. In case there are any particularities in the pharmacovigilance system for a particular medicine for which the marketing authorization is issued, an appendix to the description of the pharmacovigilance system shall be submitted as part of the documents required for obtaining a marketing authorization. The DDPS and its appendices shall be developed in Serbian or in English.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: Submit a Risk Management Plan describing the risk management system
f.statement: The MAH must submit to the Agency a description of the risk management system in the form of an RMP, with contents per Attachment 2.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall submit to the Agency a description of the risk management system in the form of the RMP document.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the English text; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level; capped below 90 because the captured text is an English rendering of the Serbian Rulebook (original 64/2011 wording, before amendments 75/2017, 82/2017 and 107/2023).

f.title: When to submit the RMP
f.statement: The MAH must submit the RMP: with an application for a new active substance, a biosimilar, or a generic where the reference product has a safety risk requiring additional minimisation; with specific variations (e.g. new strength, new route, change in manufacturing of a biotech medicine, significant indication change).
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Submission operations; Signal management

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall submit to the Agency the RMP: 1) Together with the application for issuing an authorization to market a medicine which contains a new active substance; for a biologically similar medicine; for a generic medicine when in terms of the reference medicine existence of a safety risk has been determined which shall require additional activities for its minimization; 2) With specific requests for a variation (e.g. new strength of a medicine, new route of administration, changes in the manufacturing process of a biotechnical medicine, a significant change in the indication);

f.title: Submit the RMP on Agency request or when a specific safety signal is identified

f.title: Define ADR reporting responsibilities in the PASS protocol; report per study type
f.statement: The MAH must define in the protocol responsibilities for reporting all ADRs from the PASS. Interventional PASS: report per the Rulebook on pharmacovigilance in clinical trials. Non-interventional PASS: depending on the protocol, the MAH reports under Article 17 or the investigator under Article 8.

rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall in the trial protocol determine responsibilities of reporting all adverse reactions resulting from PASS. If PASS represents a non-interventional (pharmacoepidemiological) trial, depending on how it is defined by the trial protocol, the marketing authorization holder shall report adverse reactions in accordance with Article 17 of the Rulebook, or the investigator, in accordance with Article 8 of the Rulebook.

f.title: DHCP: no advertising; send for significant safety changes
f.statement: A Direct Healthcare Professional Communication (DHCP) sent by the MAH must contain information for safe and effective use and no advertising. A DHCP is sent for significant SmPC changes (new contraindications, reduced dose, restricted indication, new warnings, new significant ADRs etc.), withdrawal or suspension of the authorisation for safety reasons, and other cases relevant to safe use.
f.clause: II.11 Letter to health care professionals, Articles 31-32

rows.quote: The DHCP shall not contain any elements of advertising a medicine. Article 32 The DHCP shall be sent in the following cases: 1) Significant amendments in the summary of product characteristics (e.g. new contraindications, reduced recommended dosage, indication restriction, restrictions in the method of issuance of a medicine, new warnings and precautions, new significant adverse reactions which may jeopardise patient’s safety, etc); 2) Withdrawal of the marketing authorization for safety reasons; 3) Suspension of the marketing authorization for safety reasons; 4) Other cases relevant for safe administration of a medicine.

f.title: Initiate urgent safety measures and inform the Agency immediately in writing
f.statement: When the MAH learns of a risk to public health from use of a medicine, it must initiate urgent safety measures and immediately inform the Agency in writing; if the Agency sends no comments within 24 hours of the notification, the measures are treated as accepted. Urgent measures apply to benefit-risk changes requiring market withdrawal, SmPC changes (contraindications, warnings, dose reduction, indication restriction) or informing HCPs and patients of new risks without delay.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Safety communications; Submission operations

rows.deadline: Inform the Agency immediately; tacit acceptance after 24 hours without Agency comments
rows.quote: The marketing authorization holder shall, in case he or she learns that there is a risk to the public health during administration of a medicine, initiate introduction of urgent safety measures, and he or she shall be responsible to immediately inform the Agency about this in writing. If the Agency sends no comments within 24 hours from the moment of receiving a written notification, the urgent safety measures referred to in paragraph 1 of the Article, shall be treated as accepted.

f.title: Sponsor: events that must be reported to the Agency
f.statement: A sponsor authorised to conduct an interventional trial in Serbia must report: SUSARs in the trial; serious expected ADRs with clinically significant increased frequency; serious risks to patients (e.g. lack of efficacy in life-threatening conditions); SUSARs after study completion reported by the investigator; and SUSARs to an active comparator (which the sponsor also notifies to the comparator's Serbian MAH). In a multicentre trial also run in Serbia, SUSARs from other countries must be reported, and all relevant safety information from other trials of the medicine submitted.

rows.quote: The sponsor who has an authorization to conduct an interventional clinical trial of a medicine in the Republic of Serbia shall report to the Agency the following as mandatory: 1) Serious, unexpected adverse reactions which occurred in a clinical trial; 2) Serious, expected adverse reactions which occurred in a clinical trial of a medicine, but with an increased frequency of occurrence (clinically significant); 3) Serious risks for patients which occurred in a clinical trial of a medicine (e.g. lack of efficacy of a medicine for patients in a life-threatening condition); 4) Serious, unexpected adverse reactions which occurred in patients after completion of a clinical study, which the investigator reported to the sponsor; 5) Serious, unexpected adverse reactions to a medicine used as active control, which the sponsor shall notify of the marketing authorization holder on the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

f.title: SUSAR initial report minimum content
f.statement: The initial SUSAR report must contain at least: the participant identification code; information on the investigational and suspect medicine; the serious unexpected event suspected to be related; the trial identification number; and the sponsor's name and address.

f.statement: If case information is incomplete, the sponsor must actively gather from the investigator all information needed for causality assessment. The follow-up report must contain: trial details (protocol number, phase, purpose, IMP, indication, authorisation number); participant initials, code, age, gender, weight, height, country; suspect medicine (INN/trade name, batch, indication, form and strength, dosing, route, start/stop dates and times); adverse reactions; concomitant medicines (including OTC, traditional, homeopathic, diet products); reporter details; sponsor details and date SUSAR was reported to the sponsor.

f.statement: The adverse reaction information must include: detailed description of all reactions, seriousness and criteria, and where possible ICD-10 diagnoses; start and stop dates and times; corrective therapy and measures; dechallenge and rechallenge information; outcome (with cause of death, causality comment and post-mortem findings if available); and information relevant to assessment (history, lab results, allergies, pregnancy, drug or alcohol abuse, family history).

f.title: Unblind only the affected participant before reporting a SUSAR
f.statement: For a SUSAR possibly related to the investigational medicine, the sponsor must break the code only for the affected participant before reporting. If the IMP or placebo was given, the suspected SUSAR is reported; if the active control was given, expectedness is reassessed against the protocol-specified SmPC and reported if unexpected.

rows.quote: In case of a serious, unexpected adverse reaction to a medicine that may have a causal link with the investigational medicine, the sponsor shall disclose a therapy code only for the trial participant with an exhibited adverse reaction, before submitting a report to the Agency. If with disclosing a therapy code is determined that the investigational medicine or placebo have been administered to the trial participant, suspected serious and unexpected adverse reactions to a medicine shall be reported to the Agency. If with disclosing a therapy code is determined that a medicine, which is active control, has been administered to the trial participant, the expectancy of an adverse reaction shall be re-assessed according to the summary of product characteristics determined in the trial protocol. If a serious adverse reaction is assessed as unexpected, it shall be reported to the Agency.

f.title: Written procedures required for core PV activities
f.statement: The DDPS must specify written procedures for: RPV activities and back-up; collection, processing, control, coding, classification, medical assessment and reporting of ICSRs (local and foreign separately); follow-up requests; duplicate detection; emergency reporting; PSUR preparation, QC, assessment and submission; continuous safety profile monitoring (signals, benefit-risk, notifying authorities and HCPs); link between safety and quality defects; responses to and execution of authority requests; urgent safety measures and variations; database use; internal supervision; training; archiving.
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Training & competency; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: It is necessary to specify for which of the following activities require written procedures: - Activities of the person responsible for pharmacovigilance in the Republic of Serbia and support system in case of absence of the responsible person; - Collecting, processing, control, coding, classification, medical assessment and reporting on individual cases of adverse reactions to a medicine (separately stated for local reports and reports on adverse reactions to a medicine from other countries); - Request for additional information on reported adverse reactions to a medicine; - Detecting duplicate reports of adverse reactions to a medicine;

f.title: Contract partner information as a DDPS appendix per application
f.statement: The DDPS must list main PV contractual relationships; since contract partners may differ per product, the MAH must present contract partner information as an appendix to the DDPS for each application (MA, variation, renewal), attached in Module 1, item 1.8.1.

rows.quote: Considering that the information about contract partners may be different for every finished medicine, the marketing authorization holder in the Republic of Serbia shall present the information about contract partners in the form of an appendix to the Detailed Description of Pharmacovigilance System for each individual request, which in the process of issuing a marketing authorization and/or amendment and/or renewal of a marketing authorization, shall be attached to the Module 1, item 1.8.1.

f.title: PV training also for sales and promotion staff
f.statement: Training on pharmacovigilance should be attended not only by employees directly involved in PV but also by all employees involved in sale and/or promotion of the MAH's medicines; the DDPS describes training content and where training records, CVs and job descriptions are archived.

rows.quote: It is necessary to describe the contents of the training and state where the training records, CVs and job descriptions shall be archived. The training on pharmacovigilance should be attended not only by the employees who are directly involved in pharmacovigilance, but also by all the employees involved in the sale and/or promotion of the medicines of the marketing authorization holder.

f.title: Supporting documents (SOPs) available and submitted on request
f.statement: The DDPS must demonstrate that the PV system exists and is documented; supporting documents such as SOPs are not enclosed but must be available and submitted at the Agency's request. Product-specific procedures should be in an appendix submitted with MA, variation or renewal applications.

rows.quote: The Detailed Description of Pharmacovigilance System shall demonstrate that such a system exists and that is has been accordingly documented. The supporting documents shall not be enclosed (SOP, etc), however, it must be available and submitted at the request of the Agency.

f.title: RMP structure and contents
f.statement: The RMP must contain a safety specification (non-clinical, clinical, unstudied populations, post-marketing experience, identified and potential risks, interactions, epidemiology, class effects, overdose, infectious transmission, abuse and off-label potential, summary of safety concerns), a pharmacovigilance plan, an assessment of the need for risk minimisation, a risk minimisation plan where additional activities apply, a summary and contact details, with appendices. Educational programmes must not contain advertising.

rows.quote: Part I: 1. Safety specification 2. Pharmacovigilance plan Part II: 3. Assessment of the need for conducting risk minimization activities 4. Risk minimization plan

f.title: Educational programmes must not contain advertising
f.statement: Educational programmes in the RMP must not contain any form of advertising of the medicine.

rows.quote: Educational program shall not contain any form of advertising a medicine.

f.title: PSUR cover page and contents
f.statement: The PSUR must have a cover page (trade name, name and address of the preparing entity, IBD, reporting period, date of document) and contain an abstract and sections on: introduction; worldwide authorisation status; safety actions; changes to reference safety information; patient exposure; individual case histories with line listings and summary tabulations; studies; other information including lack of efficacy and RMP; overall safety evaluation; and conclusion.

rows.quote: PSUR shall contain a cover page with the following information: 1) The trade name of a medicine; 2) The name and address of the legal entity which created the PSUR on the basis of manufacturer’s data; 3) The international birth date (IBD); 4) The period covered by the periodical report; 5) The date of development of the document.

f.title: PSUR case terminology: WHO-ART and/or MedDRA, reporter's terms retained
f.statement: In PSUR case descriptions, adverse reaction terminology should follow WHO-ART and/or MedDRA, with mandatory use of the terminology used by the primary reporter, and may use the appropriate ICD-10 diagnosis for a symptom complex.

f.title: Enclose the reference safety document and list SmPC vs RSI differences in the cover letter
f.statement: The PSUR includes the manufacturer's reference document with the reference safety information used; the cover letter enclosed with the PSUR must contain all relevant differences between the last approved SmPC and the applicable reference safety information.

rows.quote: Additionally, the cover letter, which shall be enclosed to the PSUR, shall contain all relevant differences between the last approved summary of product characteristics and applicable reference safety information.

f.title: Summary Bridging Report: no new information; PSUR format
f.statement: A Summary Bridging Report summarises two or more PSURs (or PSURs and Addendum Report), contains no new information, follows the PSUR format with the prescribed sections, and its cover letter must state differences between the approved SmPC and the reference safety information.

rows.quote: The Summary Bridging Report shall provide a short incorporated overview of two or more PSURs or PSURs and Addendum Report, and it shall not contain any new information.

f.title: Addendum Report: when and what to submit
f.statement: An Addendum Report complements the last PSUR when the Agency needs safety information outside the routine cycle; it is submitted three months or more after the DLP of the last 6-monthly or annual PSUR and/or six months or more after the DLP of a PSUR covering over one year, covers data from the last DLP to the date required by the Agency, and has PSUR or simplified format.

rows.quote: The Addendum Report shall represent a complement to the last PSUR and shall be developed in case the Agency needs to be submitted with an appendix on safety information in addition to the usual cycle of submissions of PSURs. The Addenda Report shall be submitted three months or more after the DLP of the last biannual or annual PSUR and/or six months or more after the DLP of the last PSUR that covers a period over one year.

f.title: Annual Safety Report structure for clinical trials
f.statement: The Annual Safety Report must have three parts: an analysis of trial participant safety with benefit-risk reassessment; a line listing of all serious adverse reactions (including SUSARs) worldwide in the trial, by MedDRA SOC, each participant once; and summary tabulations of serious adverse reactions by organ system, reaction and treatment group.

rows.quote: The Annual Safety Report for a clinical trial shall consist of the following three parts: - Part I: Analysis of the safety of trial participants in the relevant clinical trial; - Part II: Line listing of all serious adverse reactions (including all serious unexpected adverse reactions) which have occurred in the relevant clinical trial, including those occurring in the world; - Part III: A summary table overview of all serious adverse reactions occurring in the relevant trial.

f.title: One joint Annual Safety Report for several trials of the same medicine
f.statement: A sponsor conducting several trials with the same medicine in Serbia and/or the EU must prepare one joint Annual Safety Report covering all trials, with a short global safety analysis and the annual safety reports for each trial.

rows.quote: In case the sponsor conducts several trials with the same medicine in the Republic of Serbia and/or European Union, he or she shall be responsible to prepare one joint Annual Safety Report which shall include all trials.
